title: Temperature sensing in Tb3+/Eu3+-based tetranuclear silsesquioxane cages with tunable emission

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: tetraethylammonium bis(tetraphenylcyclotetrasiloxanolate) tetranuclear terbium(III)–europium(III) nitrate hydroxide ethanol aqua cage ethanol solvate

synthesis.procedure: Compounds 1 and 2 were prepared similarly. PhSi(OMe)3 and NaOH were dissolved in 30 mL of ethanol and heated to reflux for 1.0 h. Then a mixture of Tb(NO3)3·6H2O and Eu(NO3)3·6H2O in a 3/1 ratio for 1 together with Et4NCl, dissolved in 30 mL of CH3CN, was added at once. The mixture was heated to reflux for 3 h, filtered from the insoluble part, and the colorless solution was slowly evaporated (ethanol/CH3CN) over 5–10 days to give crystalline material. Single crystals were collected for SCXRD; the product was dried in vacuum for elemental analysis and yield determination. Reactant loadings for 1: PhSi(OMe)3 (0.186 g, 0.8 mmol), NaOH (0.032 g, 0.8 mmol), Tb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.131 g, 0.3 mmol), Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (0.045 g, 0.1 mmol), Et4NCl (0.066 g, 0.4 mmol).

properties.summary: Solid-state magnetic data are consistent with 75% Tb3+ occupation of the tetranuclear core (Eu3+ treated as diamagnetic). Photoluminescence shows characteristic Tb3+ (543 nm, 5D4→7F5) and Eu3+ (612 nm, 5D0→7F2) emissions with intramolecular Tb3+-to-Eu3+ energy transfer. Compound 1 functions as a ratiometric luminescent thermometer using the 543/612 nm LIR, with excellent linearity (R2 = 0.9990) and repeatability (>95%) over 41–100 °C and a maximum relative thermal sensitivity of 0.63 % °C−1 at 68 °C.

properties.summary: Magnetic data match 50% Tb3+ occupation of the tetranuclear core. Room-temperature excitation/emission of 2 differ from 1, with a lower green-to-red (543/612 nm) LIR under 378 nm excitation, consistent with more Eu3+ and intramolecular Tb3+-to-Eu3+ energy transfer. Compound 2 is also discussed as a self-referenced luminescent temperature sensor, but with lower thermal sensitivity than 1 because of stronger relative Eu3+ red emission.
